name: Temperate deciduous / mixed forest
notes: Broadleaf deciduous forest dominated by oaks, beech, maples and ash with a hazel/spicebush shrub layer and a spring-ephemeral herb carpet; drawn on lowland Europe, the eastern USA and temperate East Asia (Japan/China).

canopy.name: Oak
canopy.source: Quercus robur, pedunculate oak, Europe to Caucasus, lowland deciduous forest, 20-35 m — Kew POWO / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Red oak
canopy.source: Quercus rubra, northern red oak, eastern North America, mesic deciduous forest, 20-35 m, brilliant red autumn — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Beech
canopy.source: Fagus sylvatica, European beech, western & central Europe, shade-tolerant climax forest on well-drained soils, 25-40 m — Wikipedia / EUFORGEN

canopy.name: Maple
canopy.source: Acer saccharum, sugar maple, northeastern North America, mesic hardwood forest, 25-35 m, orange-red autumn — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

canopy.name: Ash
canopy.source: Fraxinus excelsior, European ash, Europe to SW Asia, mixed deciduous woodland on base-rich soils, 20-35 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

canopy.name: Elm
canopy.source: Ulmus americana, American elm, eastern North America, bottomland and mixed deciduous forest, 20-30 m vase shape — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Hazel
shrub.source: Corylus avellana, common hazel, Europe & W Asia, understory of oak/ash woodland, 3-8 m multi-stemmed — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Spicebush
shrub.source: Lindera benzoin, northern spicebush, eastern North America, understory of moist deciduous forest, 2-4 m, yellow spring flowers — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

shrub.name: Hawthorn
shrub.source: Crataegus monogyna, common hawthorn, Europe/NW Africa/W Asia, woodland edge and scrub, 4-8 m thorny, red haws — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

shrub.name: Moso bamboo
shrub.source: Phyllostachys edulis, moso bamboo, native to China (Taiwan), naturalised Japan, warm-temperate hill forest, culms 10-20 m — Wikipedia / Flora of China

shrub.name: Elderberry
shrub.source: Sambucus nigra, elder, Europe & W Asia, woodland edges and clearings on nitrogen-rich soil, 3-6 m, cream flower heads — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Spring herbs
ground.source: Anemone nemorosa, wood anemone, Europe, spring-ephemeral carpet of deciduous woodland floor, 10-25 cm white flowers — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Bluebell
ground.source: Hyacinthoides non-scripta, common bluebell, Atlantic Europe, dense spring carpets in oak/beech woods, 20-50 cm, violet-blue — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

ground.name: Mayapple
ground.source: Podophyllum peltatum, mayapple, eastern North America, colonies on moist deciduous forest floor, 30-50 cm umbrella leaves — USDA Plants / Wikipedia

ground.name: Lady fern
ground.source: Athyrium filix-femina, lady fern, circumboreal temperate forests, moist shaded ground, fronds 0.5-1.2 m — Wikipedia / USDA Plants

ground.name: Kuma bamboo grass
ground.source: Sasa veitchii, kuma-zasa, Japan, dwarf bamboo carpet under temperate deciduous forest, 0.5-1.5 m, leaves edged white in winter — Wikipedia / Flora of Japan

ground.name: Wood sorrel
ground.source: Oxalis acetosella, wood sorrel, Europe & N Asia, shade herb of beech/oak woodland floor, 5-10 cm — Wikipedia / Kew POWO

epiphyte.name: Ivy
epiphyte.source: Hedera helix, common ivy, Europe & W Asia, climbs trunks of oak/ash woodland up to 25 m — Wikipedia / Kew POWO
